Answer: D
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates rightward mediastinal shift and reduced right hemithorax volume, accompanied by a curvilinear "scimitar" vein in the right cardiophrenic angle. These findings, along with the appearance of the remaining right lung tissue filling the space (compensatory hyperaeration), are characteristic of Scimitar syndrome associated with right upper lobe hypoplasia.
